problem_markdown: A convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ has line $CD$ tangent to the circle with diameter $AB$. Prove that line $AB$ is tangent to the circle with diameter $CD$ exactly when $BC\parallel AD$.
solutions_markdown:
If $AB\parallel CD$, their distance equals $AB/2$ by the given tangency. The reverse tangency holds exactly when $CD=AB$, which for this convex quadrilateral is exactly the parallelogram condition $BC\parallel AD$.

Otherwise let the supporting lines meet at $O$. Convexity puts each segment on one ray from $O$; reversing the vertex labels if necessary, their orders are $O,A,B$ and $O,D,C$. Let $\theta$ be the angle between the rays. The given tangency says that the distance of the midpoint of $AB$ to line $CD$ equals $AB/2$, namely
$$\sin\theta=\frac{OB-OA}{OB+OA}.$$
The reverse tangency is equivalent to
$$\sin\theta=\frac{OC-OD}{OC+OD}.$$
These two equations are equivalent to $OA/OB=OD/OC$. By the intercept theorem this is equivalent to $AD\parallel BC$.
